title: Reward Hacking Detection via Behavioral Fingerprinting

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear chain: lightweight behavioral fingerprints during RL training could serve as early-warning indicators for reward hacking, enabling practitioners to intervene before misalignment propagates. Directly addresses a core RLHF limitation.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running an RL fine-tuning loop from scratch is significantly complex for beginners. Setting up PPO/RLHF training, defining reward models, and tracking behavioral metrics across training steps requires substantial infrastructure and experience beyond beginner level.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires: (1) setting up RLHF training, (2) defining behavioral fingerprints, (3) identifying reward hacking checkpoints, (4) correlating fingerprints with hacking onset. Multiple moving parts. Likely exceeds 30 hours for beginners.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
